subject.title: The transported classes define a subgroupoid

object.title: The transported classes define a subgroupoid

proof_context.bookkeeping: `End.of` regards a groupoid endomorphism at the basepoint as an element of its vertex group. Composition and group multiplication have reversed notation: `f ≫ g` is the product `g * f`.
proof_context.conclusion: The morphisms with transported loop class in $H$ form a subgroupoid $S$.
proof_context.explanation: The inverse and composition fields use closure of $H$ under inverses and multiplication. In the composition case, the connecting path at the middle object cancels with its inverse.

snippet.text:
let S : Subgroupoid (_root_.FundamentalGroupoid X) :=
    { arrows := fun c d ↦ {f | (End.of (τ c ≫ f ≫ inv (τ d)) : _root_.FundamentalGroup X x) ∈ H}
      inv := fun {c d f} hf ↦ by
        have h := H.inv_mem hf
        rw [hinv] at h
        simpa [Groupoid.inv_eq_inv] using h
      mul := fun {c d e f} hf {g} hg ↦ by
        have h := H.mul_mem hg hf
        -- This constructs `S`, so no membership lemma for its arrow predicate exists yet.
        -- Expose that predicate on the composite before comparing it with the product in `H`.
        change (End.of (τ c ≫ (f ≫ g) ≫ inv (τ e)) : _root_.FundamentalGroup X x) ∈ H
        convert h using 1
        ext
        simp }
